bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or have a salary offer, understanding your annual pay helps you budget and compare opportunities. The basic formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the calculation is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This gives you your gross annual income before tax, super, and any deductions. The same formula works for part-time or casual workers – just use your actual weekly hours.

### Why 38 Hours?

The Fair Work Commission sets the standard full-time week at 38 hours for the National Minimum Wage. Many awards and agreements also use 38 hours. If your hours differ, adjust the weekly figure. For example, a 40-hour week would use 40 instead of 38.

### Fortnightly Pay

If you are paid fortnightly, your gross fortnightly pay is your weekly pay multiplied by two. For a 38-hour week, that is hourly rate × 38 × 2. Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing salary packages.

## National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Many industries have award rates that are higher. Check the [pay guides](/blog) for your industry. If you are covered by an award, your minimum hourly rate may be above the national minimum.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using [the timesheet](/), enter your base hourly rate and select the casual loading checkbox – do not type a rate that already includes the loading. The calculator will add the 25% automatically.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional payment your employer makes into your super fund. It is not deducted from your pay. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual ordinary earnings are $80,000, your employer pays an extra $9,600 into super. This is on top of your gross salary. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay is your gross pay minus tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a detailed estimate.

## Comparing to the Average Salary in Vietnam

While the average salary in Vietnam is significantly lower than Australian wages, it is not directly comparable due to different cost of living and economic conditions. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings average $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). In contrast, the average salary in Vietnam is not published by the ABS, and we do not have a precise figure for this article. However, you can use our conversion tools to see how your hourly rate translates to annual pay and compare it to any benchmark you have. For a broader perspective, see [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for Australian averages.

## Important Notes

This annual pay estimate assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For more detailed calculations, refer to the [reference tables](/data) or the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide.
